18. What happens in memory when a constructor is executed?
When a constructor is invoked during object creation:
The object is created in heap memory.
A stack frame or activation record is created for the constructor.
Constructor parameters exist in that activation record.
The constructor initializes the object's instance variables.
The constructor's activation record is removed when execution finishes.
19. Does a constructor get an activation record when it is called?
A constructor executes similarly to other executable members in this respect: when it is called, an activation record or stack frame is created for its execution.
When the constructor finishes, that activation record is removed.
20. When is the reference to a newly created object assigned to the reference variable?
The object is created and its constructor executes first. After construction finishes, the reference to the object is assigned to the reference variable.
